title: Highest-Protein Fish: A Clear Ranking per 100 Grams

seo.title: Highest-Protein Fish per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Compare cooked tuna, mackerel, trout, swordfish, cod and salmon by protein, calories and serving, with clear mercury context.
seo.search_intent: Compare cooked fish by protein without mixing canned and fresh products.

excerpt: Cooked yellowfin tuna provides about 29.2 g protein per 100 g. Mackerel, trout, swordfish, cod and salmon cluster around 22–24 g, with larger differences in fat and calories than protein.
content_html:
Most fish are high-protein foods. To keep the comparison easy to read, the main table uses cooked fish. Canned fish is discussed separately because oil, salt and draining change the product substantially.

Cooked fish protein ranking

FishProtein/100 gCalories/100 g
Yellowfin tuna29.2 g130
Atlantic mackerel23.9 g262
Farmed rainbow trout23.8 g168
Swordfish23.5 g172
Wild rainbow trout22.9 g150
Atlantic cod22.8 g105
Farmed Atlantic salmon22.1 g206
Haddock20.0 g90

Mackerel, trout, swordfish and cod are very close in protein —about 22.8–23.9 g/100 g— while their fat and calorie content differ much more.

Tuna

Cooked yellowfin tuna provides about 29.2 g protein and 130 calories per 100 g. It is lean and highly protein-dense.

Mercury varies by tuna species. FDA/EPA advice places canned light tuna in the “Best Choices” category and albacore/white tuna in “Good Choices,” while bigeye tuna is in “Choices to Avoid” for people who are pregnant or breastfeeding and for children. That distinction is more useful than treating all tuna as one food.

Mackerel and salmon

Atlantic mackerel provides about 23.9 g protein and 262 calories/100 g; farmed Atlantic salmon about 22.1 g and 206 calories. Cod provides a similar 22.8 g protein with only 105 calories.

The extra calories in mackerel and salmon largely come from fat, including EPA and DHA omega-3s.

Trout

Farmed rainbow trout is around 23.8 g protein/100 g and wild rainbow trout around 22.9 g. A 5-ounce / 142 g serving provides roughly 34 and 33 g protein.

Swordfish

Swordfish provides about 23.5 g protein/100 g, very similar to trout and mackerel. FDA/EPA classifies swordfish as a “Choice to Avoid” for pregnant or breastfeeding people and young children because of mercury.

Cod and haddock

Cod provides 22.8 g protein and 105 calories/100 g; haddock roughly 20 g and 90 calories. Both are very lean.

Salted cod is a different product because curing removes water and greatly increases sodium. Once desalted it changes again, so it should not be treated as identical to simply cooked fresh cod.

Canned sardines and anchovies

Drained canned sardines in oil provide about 24.6 g protein/100 g; drained anchovies can approach 28.9 g/100 g. Their lower water content raises protein concentration.

Sardines with edible bones also provide substantial calcium. Anchovies are very high in sodium, and a normal serving is small: 20 g of anchovies provides about 5.8 g protein, not 28.9 g.

Protein by serving

FishServingProtein
Cooked tuna5 oz / 142 g41 g
Mackerel5 oz / 142 g34 g
Trout5 oz / 142 g34 g
Cod5 oz / 142 g32 g
Salmon5 oz / 142 g31 g
Canned sardines3.75 oz can / ~106 g~26 g

White vs oily fish

The white/oily distinction does not predict protein well. Cod and salmon provide 22.8 and 22.1 g/100 g, almost the same. The larger difference is fat: salmon commonly has more than 10 g/100 g while cod is near 1 g.

Bottom line

Tuna is near the top for protein concentration, while many fish cluster around 20–24 g/100 g. Fatty-acid profile, mercury, calcium in edible-bone fish and sodium in canned products often matter more than a small protein difference.

Sources

Food values come from USDA FoodData Central. Mercury advice comes from FDA/EPA Advice about Eating Fish.

faq.question: Which fish has the most protein?
faq.answer: Among the cooked fish compared here, yellowfin tuna is about 29.2 g/100 g. Mackerel, trout, swordfish and cod are around 22.8–23.9 g.

faq.question: Does salmon have less protein than tuna?
faq.answer: Yes in these examples: about 22.1 g/100 g versus 29.2 g for yellowfin tuna. Salmon contains much more fat, including omega-3s.

faq.question: Which fish are highest in mercury?
faq.answer: FDA/EPA places swordfish and bigeye tuna among the choices to avoid for pregnant or breastfeeding people and children.
